name: phishing_docusign_finance

trigger.description: Phishing email detected targeting Finance department. Spoofed DocuSign notification containing credential harvesting link to hxxps://docusign-verify[.]xyz/auth. One user (j.martinez) clicked the link but did not submit credentials.

indicators.subject: Action Required: Review and Sign Q1 Financial Report

expected_behavior: Full pipeline execution: detect, analyze phishing indicators, block sender domain, reset user session, generate report.

reads.query: search threat repository for similar phishing campaigns targeting finance department
recent SIEM events for source IP 93.184.216.34 and recipient j.martinez@corp.local
known credential harvesting domains similar to docusign-verify.xyz
open cases involving phishing attacks on finance department
existing playbooks for phishing response and credential harvesting
current email gateway block rules for spoofed DocuSign domains
prior remediation actions for phishing incidents in Q1 2026

writes.content: Threat assessment: DocuSign phishing campaign targeting Finance department via credential harvesting at docusign-verify.xyz. One user clicked link but did not submit credentials.
Case update INC-2026-0701: Phishing indicators confirmed — spoofed DocuSign domain, credential harvesting URL, single affected user j.martinez. No credential compromise.
Incident report INC-2026-0701: Phishing email blocked, sender domain docusign-verify.xyz added to blocklist, user session reset for j.martinez, no data loss confirmed.
Metrics update: phishing detection count incremented, mean time to detect 12 minutes, mean time to contain 28 minutes.

name: phishing_o365_credential_harvest

trigger.description: Credential harvesting campaign impersonating Microsoft 365 login page. Three users in HR department received identical emails with typosquatted domain. Two users submitted credentials before detection.

indicators.subject: Urgent: Your password expires in 24 hours

expected_behavior: Detect campaign, disable compromised accounts (s.patel, l.garcia), block sender domain, notify affected users, generate incident report.

reads.query: search threat repository for credential harvesting campaigns impersonating Microsoft 365
SIEM authentication logs for users s.patel, l.garcia, m.thompson in the last 24 hours
threat intel on typosquatted domain microsft-365.com and IP 104.21.45.67
any prior credential compromise incidents for HR department users
case management entries for compromised account remediation playbook
IAM policy for bulk account disable and credential rotation in HR OU
historical remediation records for credential harvesting campaigns
prior incident reports involving Microsoft 365 impersonation

writes.content: Threat assessment: Microsoft 365 credential harvesting campaign targeting HR department. Typosquatted domain microsft-365.com used. Two users (s.patel, l.garcia) submitted credentials before detection.
Case update INC-2026-0702: Confirmed credential compromise for s.patel and l.garcia. Accounts disabled, password rotation initiated. m.thompson received email but did not interact.
Incident report INC-2026-0702: O365 credential harvesting campaign contained. Two compromised accounts disabled, sender domain blocked, all sessions revoked.
Metrics update: credential compromise count 2, campaign scope 3 recipients, mean time to detect 18 minutes, mean time to contain 45 minutes.

name: phishing_spearphish_exec

trigger.description: CFO reported suspicious email appearing to be from the CEO requesting an urgent wire transfer. Email originated from external address using display name spoofing. No links or attachments present; pure social engineering attempt (BEC).

expected_behavior: Classify as BEC attempt, block sender domain, add to threat intelligence, notify executive team, generate report with no containment actions needed.

reads.query: search threat repository for business email compromise attempts targeting executive accounts
SIEM email flow logs for sender domain corp-executive.com and reply-to protonmail.com
known BEC campaigns using display name spoofing of CEO or CFO roles
executive impersonation attack patterns and social engineering TTPs
BEC response playbook and executive notification procedures
prior remediation actions for BEC and wire fraud attempts
previous BEC incident reports for trend analysis

writes.content: Threat assessment: Business Email Compromise attempt targeting CFO. Display name spoofing of CEO with external reply-to address (protonmail.com). Urgent wire transfer social engineering. No financial loss — CFO reported before action.
Case update INC-2026-0703: Confirmed BEC attempt. Sender domain corp-executive.com blocked. No wire transfer executed. Executive team notified of spoofing attempt.
Incident report INC-2026-0703: BEC attempt classified and contained. Sender domain blocked, threat intel updated, no financial loss. Executive awareness briefing scheduled.
Metrics update: BEC attempt count incremented, user-reported detection, zero financial loss, executive notification within 15 minutes.

name: phishing_qr_code_vishing

trigger.description: QR code phishing (quishing) campaign detected. Emails contain PDF attachment with embedded QR code linking to credential harvesting page. Five emails delivered to Engineering department before gateway rule was updated.

indicators.subject: MFA Enrollment Required - Scan QR Code

expected_behavior: Block sender, quarantine delivered emails, scan affected workstations for follow-up activity, generate report with IoCs.

reads.query: search threat repository for QR code phishing (quishing) campaigns and PDF-based delivery vectors
SIEM email delivery logs for sender it-support@corp-helpdesk.net and Engineering department recipients
known quishing infrastructure and credential harvesting domains similar to corp-mfa-setup.com
open cases for phishing campaigns targeting Engineering department
email quarantine procedures and bulk workstation scan playbooks
endpoint scan configuration for post-phishing workstation assessment
remediation records for prior quishing or QR-based phishing incidents

writes.content: Threat assessment: QR code phishing campaign targeting Engineering department. PDF attachments with embedded QR codes linking to credential harvesting at corp-mfa-setup.com. Five emails delivered before gateway rule update.
Case update INC-2026-0704: Quishing campaign confirmed. Sender blocked, delivered emails quarantined, workstation scans initiated for 5 affected endpoints. No credential submission detected.
Incident report INC-2026-0704: QR code phishing campaign contained. 5 emails quarantined, sender domain blocked, IoCs extracted and shared: corp-mfa-setup.com, it-support@corp-helpdesk.net.
Metrics update: quishing campaign detected, 5 recipients in scope, 0 credential submissions, gateway rule updated in 22 minutes.

name: phishing_html_smuggling

trigger.description: HTML smuggling attack detected. Email with HTML attachment triggered JavaScript execution that assembled and dropped an ISO file containing a malicious LNK. EDR blocked the LNK execution on the endpoint.

expected_behavior: Confirm EDR block, quarantine email, scan endpoint for persistence, block sender domain, hash ISO file for IoC sharing, generate report.

reads.query: search threat repository for HTML smuggling techniques and ISO-based payload delivery
SIEM and EDR events for endpoint WS-FIN-AP06 IP 10.0.10.60 in the last 4 hours
recent incident reports involving HTML smuggling or ISO file drops
threat intel on sender domain supplier-payments.org and C2 IP 91.234.99.41
EDR quarantine confirmation and malware analysis results for Invoice.iso
malware containment playbook for HTML smuggling with endpoint persistence check
firewall rules for blocking external IP 91.234.99.41 and domain supplier-payments.org
prior remediation actions for HTML smuggling and ISO-based attacks
IoC sharing records for similar delivery techniques

writes.content: Threat assessment: HTML smuggling attack delivering ISO payload with malicious LNK. JavaScript in HTML attachment assembled ISO file containing LNK targeting cmd.exe/powershell. EDR blocked execution on WS-FIN-AP06. C2 IP 91.234.99.41.
Case update INC-2026-0705: HTML smuggling confirmed. EDR block verified, ISO file hashed for IoC sharing, endpoint scanned for persistence — none found. Sender domain and C2 IP blocked.
Incident report INC-2026-0705: HTML smuggling attack contained by EDR. ISO payload blocked, sender domain supplier-payments.org and C2 91.234.99.41 blocked. No persistence established.
Metrics update: HTML smuggling detection by EDR, time to block 0 seconds (automated), time to full containment 35 minutes, IoC hashes shared to threat intel feed.

name: lateral_movement_smb_spray

trigger.description: SIEM correlation rule triggered: single source host attempting SMB authentication to 15 hosts within the Finance VLAN in under 3 minutes. Source host is an Engineering workstation that should not have SMB access to Finance.

expected_behavior: Isolate source host, disable d.chen account, investigate 3 successful authentications, block cross-VLAN SMB, generate report.

name: lateral_movement_psexec

trigger.description: EDR detected PsExec execution from compromised workstation to domain controller. The attacker used a stolen service account (svc-backup) to execute commands remotely on DC-PRIMARY-01. Commands included ntdsutil for Active Directory database extraction.

expected_behavior: Immediately isolate source host, disable svc-backup, check for NTDS.dit exfiltration, initiate krbtgt rotation planning, generate critical incident report.

name: lateral_movement_rdp_tunneling

trigger.description: Anomalous RDP tunneling detected. Internal host establishing RDP sessions through an SSH tunnel to reach servers in the DMZ, bypassing network segmentation controls. Traffic pattern consistent with Chisel or similar tunneling tools.

expected_behavior: Kill tunnel connection, isolate source workstation, block port 8443 on internal firewall, investigate DMZ server integrity, generate report.

name: lateral_movement_wmi_execution

trigger.description: WMI-based remote execution detected across multiple hosts. A compromised admin account is using WMI to execute encoded PowerShell commands on servers in the IT management VLAN. Commands appear to be deploying a persistence mechanism.

expected_behavior: Disable admin-deploy account, isolate source and target hosts, decode and analyze PowerShell payload, check for persistence, generate report.

name: lateral_movement_dcom_abuse

trigger.description: DCOM lateral movement detected. Attacker leveraging MMC20.Application DCOM object to execute commands on remote host via the ExecuteShellCommand method. Source is a previously compromised HR workstation.

expected_behavior: Isolate both hosts, disable s.patel account, audit Domain Admins group for unauthorized changes, harden DCOM settings, generate report.

name: malware_emotet_dropper

trigger.description: Emotet dropper detected on Finance workstation. Malicious macro in Excel document triggered download of Emotet DLL from external C2 server. EDR quarantined the payload before execution but the initial dropper document was opened.

expected_behavior: Confirm quarantine, scan for persistence, block C2 IP on firewall, submit hashes to threat intel, notify user, generate report.

name: malware_cobalt_strike_beacon

trigger.description: Cobalt Strike beacon detected performing DNS-based C2 communication. Beacon is running as an in-memory payload injected into svchost.exe on an Engineering workstation. Periodic DNS queries to randomly generated subdomains of cdn-metrics[.]cloud observed.

expected_behavior: Immediately isolate host, block C2 domain and IP, memory dump for forensic analysis, check for lateral movement, generate critical report.

name: malware_ransomware_precursor

trigger.description: Ransomware precursor activity detected on file server. Volume Shadow Copy deletion commands (vssadmin delete shadows /all) followed by attempts to disable Windows Defender via PowerShell. No encryption observed yet, indicating pre-ransomware reconnaissance.

expected_behavior: Immediately isolate file server, disable svc-backup account, verify backup integrity, block external IP, escalate as critical, generate emergency report.

name: malware_cryptominer

trigger.description: Cryptominer detected on development server. Sustained 95%+ CPU utilization from unknown process 'systemd-helper' running XMRig Monero miner. Process was deployed via compromised Jenkins build pipeline. Mining pool connection to pool.minexmr.com:443.

expected_behavior: Kill miner process, investigate Jenkins compromise, block mining pool, audit build pipeline integrity, generate report.

name: malware_infostealer_browser

trigger.description: RedLine Stealer malware detected exfiltrating browser credentials and cookies. Malware was delivered via fake Chrome update prompt from compromised website. EDR detected credential file access patterns and outbound data exfiltration to C2.

expected_behavior: Isolate host, force password reset for h.young across all services, revoke browser sessions, block C2, submit malware sample, generate report.

name: exfil_dns_tunneling

trigger.description: DNS tunneling exfiltration detected. Anomalous DNS TXT queries with high-entropy subdomain labels observed from Engineering workstation. Query volume exceeds 500 queries/minute to a single external domain. Payload encoding consistent with dnscat2 or iodine tunneling tools.

expected_behavior: Block tunneling domain, isolate source host, analyze DNS logs for exfiltrated content, assess data exposure, generate report.

name: exfil_cloud_upload

trigger.description: DLP alert triggered: large volume of classified financial documents uploaded to personal Dropbox account. User compressed 847 files from the Finance shared drive into encrypted 7z archives and uploaded 2.3 GB to cloud storage. DLP flagged PCI and PII content patterns.

expected_behavior: Block cloud upload, isolate workstation, disable user account, assess data exposure scope, initiate insider threat investigation, generate report.

name: exfil_steganography_images

trigger.description: Suspected steganographic exfiltration detected. Compromised workstation uploading unusually large image files (50-80 MB PNG files) to external image hosting service. Statistical analysis of image files shows anomalous LSB patterns consistent with data embedding.

expected_behavior: Block image hosting upload, isolate workstation, capture uploaded images for analysis, investigate source of embedded data, generate report.

name: exfil_email_forwarding_rule

trigger.description: Mailbox forwarding rule detected on executive assistant account. All emails containing keywords 'merger', 'acquisition', 'board', 'confidential' are being auto-forwarded to external Gmail address. Rule was created 72 hours ago, estimated 340 emails forwarded.

expected_behavior: Remove forwarding rule, reset account credentials, audit all forwarded emails, block external address, investigate rule creation source IP, generate report.

name: exfil_database_dump

trigger.description: Unauthorized database dump detected on production SQL server. Service account svc-sql-prod executed mysqldump against the customer_records database (4.2 million rows) at 3 AM. The dump was compressed and staged in /tmp on the database server. Outbound SCP transfer to external IP initiated but blocked by firewall.

expected_behavior: Disable svc-sql-prod account, delete staged dump file, block external IP, audit database access logs, assess data exposure, generate critical report.
